overview: South Sudan became independent from Sudan on 9 July 2011 after a referendum. This map’s modern-country layer begins only in 2020, so its first displayed year is not the country’s founding date. Older communities and histories also extend across the border separating the two modern states.

periods.title: Independence before the map layer
periods.summary: The referendum and declaration of independence created a separate republic before this record’s displayed coverage.

periods.title: Civil war and displacement
periods.summary: Conflict beginning in December 2013 brought severe civilian suffering and a greater emphasis on protection.

periods.title: Peace agreement and an unfinished transition
periods.summary: A revitalized agreement set out a route toward peace; renewed confrontation was still being reported in 2025.

sections.title: A new country with older histories

items.text: The 2005 Comprehensive Peace Agreement set the path toward a vote on southern Sudan’s future. In January 2011, voters overwhelmingly chose separation, and independence followed that July. South Sudan and Sudan therefore became distinct countries, while families and historical connections continued across the new international boundary.

Fighting broke out in December 2013, only two years after independence. The United Nations strengthened its mission’s civilian-protection role. A revitalized peace agreement was signed in September 2018, but signing a document was one step in a difficult process of making communities safe.

Here is Juba Arabic in the scholarly spelling recorded by linguists: “ána kan déru áynu akú tái”, translated “I wanted to see my brother.” The Latin letters and accents reproduce an attested modern transcription. This small family sentence offers a language sample without pretending it is an ancient inscription.

sections.title: Saving records and making history public

items.text: War left many administrative records damaged, scattered or stored in sacks in damp rooms. Archivists and their partners worked to clean, sort, box and digitize surviving papers from the colonial period through the 1980s. Sometimes preserving history starts with the distinctly unglamorous job of rescuing a pile of paper.

In November 2017, the Tarikh Tana radio series brought archival documents into public conversation. South Sudanese panelists discussed a different document each week on Eye Radio, alongside exhibitions. History could be heard on a radio as well as read in an archive, reaching people beyond a reading room.

sections.title: School, water and skilled local work

items.text: A 2021 education case study describes repairs to girls’ latrines and installation of handwashing facilities at two schools in Torit County. These changes helped pupils manage everyday needs, including menstruation. Returning to class after COVID-19 closures involved usable toilets and privacy as well as reopening school gates.

The same programme supported mothers’ groups and girls’ clubs. Older female pupils trained to encourage others to return to school and to speak up about education. Learning was supported by relationships across generations: classmates and mothers could help address concerns that a textbook alone could not solve.

Yei’s upgraded water system opened in May 2023 with five boreholes, 59 water kiosks and about 33 kilometres of pipe. Solar power ran the system, and chlorination helped keep the water safe. Water services need pumps, treatment and maintenance together; sunshine alone cannot make a dirty cup clean.

At Boma Hospital, solar equipment installed in late 2022 supplied lights and reliable power for vaccine storage. In a May 2023 report, staff described easier night-time deliveries and better temperature control. Electricity changed very practical tasks: seeing a patient clearly and keeping essential medicines appropriately cool.

In a 2025 account from Mangaten, 21-year-old Veronica interpreted for a women’s support group while studying international relations in Juba. The programme combined emotional support with skills such as making soap and weaving baskets for sale. Her story shows education, care and earning a living meeting in one person’s working week.

At the Paris 2024 Olympic tournament, South Sudan’s men won their first Olympic basketball game, defeating Puerto Rico 90 to 79 in Lille. Nuni Omot scored the country’s first Olympic basketball points. A young state could now add an international sporting achievement to the stories told about it.

The win required more than one star. Carlik Jones recorded 19 points, seven rebounds and six assists, while four teammates also scored at least ten points. South Sudan collected 55 rebounds against Puerto Rico’s 37. A missed shot was often the beginning of another chance, not the end of the play.

ending.text: South Sudan continues as an independent country. In April 2025, UN officials warned that renewed military confrontation threatened the peace process. That dated warning shows why the 2018 agreement should not be presented as a complete end to violence, even as citizens continue schooling, research, work and cultural life.
